title: Fesenjan (Chicken in Walnut and Pomegranate Sauce)
summary: Chicken thighs are simmered gently in a slow-cooked walnut and pomegranate molasses sauce, served with saffron rice.
equipment: large heavy casserole (26-28 cm) with a lid

ingredients.note: only if the sauce is too sour

ingredients.item: fine sea salt or table salt
saffron threads, ground with a pinch of sugar and steeped in 2 tbsp hot water
fine sea salt or table salt, for the rice water

steps.title: Toast and grind the walnuts
steps.text: Toast the walnuts in a dry pan over medium heat for 5-7 minutes, shaking often, until fragrant and a shade darker, then let them cool and pulse in a food processor to a fine, sandy meal rather than a paste.

steps.title: Soften the onion
steps.text: Heat the oil in the casserole over medium heat and cook the onion with a pinch of salt for 10-12 minutes until soft and golden. Add the turmeric and cinnamon for 30 seconds until fragrant.

steps.title: Build the walnut sauce
steps.text: Stir in the ground walnuts and cook for 2 minutes, then add the water or stock, pomegranate molasses and salt. Bring to a simmer, cover partly, and cook gently for 45-60 minutes, stirring every 10 minutes so it doesn't catch, until the sauce darkens to a deep brown and a thin layer of walnut oil pools on the surface - a sign the sauce has fully developed.

steps.title: Add the chicken
steps.text: Season the chicken with the pepper and add it to the sauce. Cover and simmer gently for 25-30 minutes until tender and the chicken reaches at least 74°C (165°F) (80°C (175°F) makes the thighs especially tender).

steps.title: Adjust the seasoning
steps.text: Taste the sauce - it should be a balance of sour and sweet. Add the sugar or honey only if it tastes too sharp, a little more molasses if it's flat, and loosen with water if it's too thick.

steps.title: Cook the saffron rice
steps.text: Rinse the basmati rice until the water runs clear, then boil in salted water for 6-7 minutes until just tender and drain. Return it to the pan with the butter and 2 tablespoons of water, cover with a lid wrapped in a clean tea towel (keep the cloth well away from the flame), and steam on low heat for 20 minutes. Drizzle the saffron water over a few spoonfuls of the cooked rice to make golden grains for the top.

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Serve the stew scattered with pomegranate seeds, with the saffron rice alongside.

tips: Grind the toasted walnuts to a fine, sandy texture rather than a paste, so they thicken the sauce evenly without turning it oily.
Common mistake: rushing the long simmer. The sauce needs the full 45-60 minutes to darken and for the walnut oil to separate out, which is key to its flavour.
Stir the sauce regularly during the long simmer, as the ground walnuts can catch and stick to the base of the pan.
Taste before adding sugar or honey - fesenjan should stay noticeably tart, not sweet.
Steaming the rice with a towel under the lid helps trap steam and keeps the grains fluffy rather than sticky.
storage: Keep in the fridge for up to 3 days or freeze for up to 2 months; the flavour often improves overnight. Reheat gently on the hob, stirring often, until piping hot throughout (74°C (165°F)). Cool leftovers in a shallow container and refrigerate within 2 hours (1 hour on a day above 32°C (90°F)).
